review_notes: Source-first scope: the paper asks whether conservatism has changed over time and lists four measure families. Equation (1)/Table 5 is the only explicitly estimated regression family; it evaluates the earnings–return association and its change across periods. The other measure families are reported through accrual summaries, distributional statistics, and market-to-book summaries rather than additional estimated equations. No fitted construction is required for Equation (1).

Section 4.3 describes average annual measures over five-year intervals, while Table 5 reports an overall fit and subperiod results with N and coefficient statistics. The supplied text does not resolve whether the equation was fit annually and averaged within each interval or pooled within each interval; the fitting procedure remains unresolved.
results_review_notes: All Equation (1) coefficient estimates and t-values are retained for the Table 5 overall period and nine subperiod columns.
Table 5 sample N, adjusted R², relative bad/good-news sensitivity, bad/good-news R² ratio, and total-bias cells are retained as auxiliary rows within their existing fit result sets.

The source states that annual b1 is equal across later and earlier years is rejected at 1%; exact test details are absent, so only the prose conclusion is retained in an auxiliary cross-period comparison record.
The source prose mean of the earnings-to-price ratio, 0.09, is retained as a dependent-variable descriptive with N/time scope left unclear; Table 1 ROA means are not linked to Equation (1) variables.
Subperiod estimation is marked unclear because Section 4.3 describes average annual measures over five-year intervals but does not resolve annual averaging versus pooled estimation.
